description:
Yazılım mühendisliği, veri analitiği ve sistem mimarisi alanlarında güçlü teknik altyapıya sahip ekibimiz; astronot sağlığı ve uzay görevlerinin kritik gereksinimlerine yönelik uçtan uca yazılım çözümleri geliştirmektedir.

İleri düzey algoritmik yaklaşımlarımızı ve problem çözme kabiliyetimizi birleştirerek, bu süreçte en yüksek standartlarda bir proje ortaya koymayı ve küresel yarışmada birinciliği elde etmeyi hedefliyoruz. Teknik disiplinimiz ve inovatif vizyonumuzla uzay teknolojilerine somut katkı sunmaya hazırız.
summary:
NASA SPACES PROE is an immersive, first-person (FPS) 3D space health monitoring and mission simulation designed to tackle the severe physiological challenges of long-duration spaceflight (Moon and Mars exploration).

In microgravity, astronauts suffer rapid bone demineralization (~1.5% per month), muscle atrophy, cardiovascular deconditioning, neuro-ocular syndrome (SANS), and cumulative cosmic radiation. While existing space missions rely heavily on Earth-bound medical telemetry, NASA SPACES PROE empowers astronauts to become autonomous caretakers of their health. Players conduct 3-phase biometric scans, monitor live vitals via a wrist holographic HUD, repair critical life-support systems, and evaluate 180-day physiological trend analytics to execute targeted countermeasures.
details:
1. Age-Stratified Astronaut Profiles:

The simulator features three archetypes (Rookie, Veteran, Senior). Derived from NASA Human Research Program (HRP) clinical datasets, deterministic mathematical multipliers simulate how age alters rates of bone mineral loss, cardiovascular strain, and circadian stress.

2. 7 Interconnected 3D Mission Scenes:

Players navigate seamlessly across Kennedy Space Center Ground Campus, Medical Diagnostic Center, Shuttle Cockpit, Orbital Transit, International Space Station (ISS), and Earth Landing. A custom lightweight kinematic and AABB collision engine ensures smooth axis-separated wall sliding, dynamic launchpad gantry stair climbing, sprinting, and jumping at 60 FPS.

3. 3-Phase Longitudinal Biometric Diagnostics:

Diagnostic booths capture 7 critical NASA HRP clinical parameters at Day 0 (Pre-Flight Baseline), Day 90 (Peak Microgravity in Orbit), and Day 180 (Earth Return Rehabilitation). The platform tracks Radiation Dose (mSv), Bone Density Loss (%), Muscle Mass Loss (%), Cardiovascular VO2 Max, Immune Competence, SANS (Ocular Pressure), and Sleep/Stress levels.

4. Emergency Systems Repair & Mission Interdependence:

Upon docking with the ISS, players must resolve critical failures in the Power Distribution Unit (PDU-1), Oxygen Generation System (OGS-2), and Ku-Band Communication Antenna. Using an interactive oscilloscope interface, astronauts calibrate frequencies to restore life support before return clearance is granted.

5. Real-Time Holographic HUD & Seamless UX:

Pressing the 'R' key projects a semi-transparent floating Holographic HUD displaying vital signs, actionable countermeasures, and NASA's 4 hazard categories. The 'Tab' key opens the mission wrist tablet. The system features automated pointer-lock management, releasing the cursor for diagnostic modals and instantly re-locking it upon closing.

6. 180-Day Longitudinal Trend Analytics:

Mission debriefing presents dynamic Recharts-powered graphs tracking 180-day physiological degradation curves mapped against selected astronaut profiles, paired with verified NASA and CSA clinical countermeasure protocols.

7. Software Architecture & Zero-Asset Procedural Audio:

Engineered with Next.js 16 (Turbopack), React Three Fiber (Three.js WebGL), TypeScript, and Zustand. The application contains zero external .mp3/.wav sound files; all footstep kinematics, airlock sweeps, alarms, and diagnostic tones are synthesized entirely in real time via the native Web Audio API. Validated by 33 passing automated Vitest tests.
dataRefs: Canadian Space Agency – Why Do We Conduct Science Experiments in Space?
